safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated allergies section is empty and does not mention penicillin allergy.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting a penicillin allergy can lead to inadvertent prescribing/administration of a beta-lactam antibiotic, which may trigger an allergic reaction ranging from rash to anaphylaxis. Allergies are high-risk safety data, and absence in the allergy list increases the chance of downstream exposure.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold supports chest tightness (hpi-003) but not wheeze; transcript documents tightness and does not clearly endorse wheeze—combined 'tightness/wheeze' overstates symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting wheeze when the patient did not clearly report it can exaggerate lower-airway involvement and potentially bias clinicians toward asthma/anaphylaxis management decisions (e.g., bronchodilators, higher perceived severity). In this case, the patient already had breathing symptoms and was directed to urgent care, so incremental harm is limited.
